description: Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.

b.request: Top 10 films ranked by how far their inventory copy counts deviate from the overall average copies per film, where both per-rating and overall averages are calculated only among films with at least one copy in inventory, displaying film_id, rating, copy_count, difference_from_rating_average, and difference_from_overall_average, sorted by overall_difference descending.
b.sql:
WITH film_copies AS (
  SELECT 
    f.film_id,
    f.rating,
    COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copy_count
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating
),
rating_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    rating,
    AVG(copy_count) AS avg_copies_per_rating
  FROM film_copies
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(copy_count) AS avg_copies_overall
  FROM film_copies
)
SELECT 
  fc.film_id,
  fc.rating,
  fc.copy_count,
  fc.copy_count - rs.avg_copies_per_rating AS difference_from_rating_average,
  fc.copy_count - os.avg_copies_overall AS difference_from_overall_average
FROM film_copies fc
JOIN rating_stats rs ON fc.rating = rs.rating
CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
ORDER BY difference_from_overall_average DESC
LIMIT 10

c.request: Which 10 films have the most inventory copies compared with the average number of copies per film? For each, show the film id, its rating, its number of copies, how far that is from the average copies per film for its rating, and how far it is from the overall average copies per film (averaged over films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the overall difference, largest first. Ties can go in any order, and nothing is rounded. Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.
c.sql:
WITH film_copies AS (
  SELECT 
    f.film_id,
    f.rating,
    COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies
  FROM film f
  LEFT JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating
  HAVING COUNT(i.inventory_id) > 0
),
rating_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    rating,
    AVG(copies) AS avg_copies_per_rating
  FROM film_copies
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(copies) AS avg_copies_overall
  FROM film_copies
)
SELECT 
  fc.film_id,
  fc.rating,
  fc.copies,
  fc.copies - ra.avg_copies_per_rating AS diff_from_rating_avg,
  fc.copies - oa.avg_copies_overall AS diff_from_overall_avg
FROM film_copies fc
JOIN rating_avg ra ON fc.rating = ra.rating
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC
LIMIT 10

d.request: Return the top 10 films ranked by inventory copy count, displaying their film ID, rating, copy count, difference from the mean copies per film for their rating (excluding films without copies), and difference from the overall mean copies per film across all films with copies, sorted by overall difference descending.
d.sql:
WITH film_copies AS (
  SELECT 
    f.film_id,
    f.rating,
    COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copy_count
  FROM film f
  LEFT JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating
  HAVING COUNT(i.inventory_id) > 0
),
rating_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    rating,
    AVG(copy_count) AS avg_copies_rating
  FROM film_copies
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(copy_count) AS avg_copies_overall
  FROM film_copies
),
top_films AS (
  SELECT 
    fc.film_id,
    fc.rating,
    fc.copy_count,
    fc.copy_count - rs.avg_copies_rating AS diff_from_rating_mean,
    fc.copy_count - os.avg_copies_overall AS diff_from_overall_mean,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY fc.copy_count DESC) AS rnk
  FROM film_copies fc
  JOIN rating_stats rs ON fc.rating = rs.rating
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
)
SELECT 
  film_id,
  rating,
  copy_count,
  diff_from_rating_mean,
  diff_from_overall_mean
FROM top_films
WHERE rnk <= 10
ORDER BY diff_from_overall_mean DESC

a.request: Looking only at films that have at least one copy in inventory (films with no copies are left out completely, including from every average), count each film's inventory copies. For each film, show its id, its rating, its number of copies, its copy count minus the average copy count per film for films of the same rating, and its copy count minus the overall average copy count per film (averaged over the individual films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the difference from the overall average, largest first, and keep the top 10 (ties broken arbitrarily). Do not round.
a.sql:
WITH film_copies AS (
  SELECT 
    f.film_id,
    f.rating,
    COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copy_count
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating
),
rating_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    rating,
    AVG(copy_count) AS avg_copies_for_rating
  FROM film_copies
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(copy_count) AS avg_copies_overall
  FROM film_copies
)
SELECT 
  fc.film_id,
  fc.rating,
  fc.copy_count,
  fc.copy_count - ra.avg_copies_for_rating AS diff_from_rating_avg,
  fc.copy_count - oa.avg_copies_overall AS diff_from_overall_avg
FROM film_copies fc
JOIN rating_avg ra ON fc.rating = ra.rating
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC
LIMIT 10
